classification.difficultyReason: Requires reversing shifts and scale factors using exponential-logarithmic equivalence, then determining natural domains from positive logarithm arguments. The hardest parts link several familiar inverse operations with a shifted domain restriction.

content.prompt: For each function $f(x)$, find its domain. Then find the inverse function $g(x)$ and its domain.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: all real numbers.

$g(x)=\dfrac{x}{3}$; domain of $g$: all real numbers.
answer.worked:
The linear rule is defined for all real $x$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=3y\\\frac{x}{3}&=y\\g(x)&=\frac{x}{3}\end{aligned}$$

The domain of $g$ is all real numbers.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: all real numbers.

$g(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\log_2 x$; domain of $g$: $x>0$.
answer.worked:
The exponential rule is defined for all real $x$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=2^{3y}\\\log_2 x&=3y\\\frac{1}{3}\log_2 x&=y\\g(x)&=\frac{1}{3}\log_2 x\end{aligned}$$

The logarithm requires $x>0$, the domain of $g$.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: all real numbers.

$g(x)=\log_7\!\left(\dfrac{x}{5}\right)$; domain of $g$: $x>0$.
answer.worked:
The exponential rule is defined for all real $x$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=5\times7^y\\\frac{x}{5}&=7^y\\\log_7\!\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)&=y\\g(x)&=\log_7\!\left(\frac{x}{5}\right)\end{aligned}$$

The logarithm requires $\frac{x}{5}>0$, so the domain of $g$ is $x>0$.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: $x>0$.

$g(x)=5^x$; domain of $g$: all real numbers.
answer.worked:
The logarithm requires $x>0$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=\log_5 y\\5^x&=y\\g(x)&=5^x\end{aligned}$$

The domain of $g$ is all real numbers.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: $x>0$.

$g(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}4^{x/2}$; domain of $g$: all real numbers.
answer.worked:
The logarithm requires $3x>0$, so the domain of $f$ is $x>0$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=2\log_4(3y)\\\frac{x}{2}&=\log_4(3y)\\4^{x/2}&=3y\\\frac{1}{3}4^{x/2}&=y\\g(x)&=\frac{1}{3}4^{x/2}\end{aligned}$$

The domain of $g$ is all real numbers.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: $x>3$.

$g(x)=2^x+3$; domain of $g$: all real numbers.
answer.worked:
The logarithm requires $x-3>0$, so the domain of $f$ is $x>3$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=\log_2(y-3)\\2^x&=y-3\\2^x+3&=y\\g(x)&=2^x+3\end{aligned}$$

The domain of $g$ is all real numbers.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: all real numbers.

$g(x)=\log_5 x+1$; domain of $g$: $x>0$.
answer.worked:
The exponential rule is defined for all real $x$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=5^{y-1}\\\log_5 x&=y-1\\\log_5 x+1&=y\\g(x)&=\log_5 x+1\end{aligned}$$

The logarithm requires $x>0$, the domain of $g$.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: $x>0$.

$g(x)=4^{x-4}$; domain of $g$: all real numbers.
answer.worked:
The logarithm requires $x>0$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=4+\log_4 y\\x-4&=\log_4 y\\4^{x-4}&=y\\g(x)&=4^{x-4}\end{aligned}$$

The domain of $g$ is all real numbers.

answer.short:
Domain of $f$: all real numbers.

$g(x)=\dfrac{1}{3}\log_5(x-5)$; domain of $g$: $x>5$.
answer.worked:
The exponential rule is defined for all real $x$.

Interchange $x$ and $y$:

$$\begin{aligned}x&=5^{3y}+5\\x-5&=5^{3y}\\\log_5(x-5)&=3y\\\frac{1}{3}\log_5(x-5)&=y\\g(x)&=\frac{1}{3}\log_5(x-5)\end{aligned}$$

The logarithm requires $x-5>0$, so the domain of $g$ is $x>5$.
